A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSCR study. The text, equations, figures, tables, and scientific Appendices A–D are readable and support a complete comparison; v2 additionally contains acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing experiments on EmbedLLM, MixInstruct, and RouterBench, including generalization tests, ablations, routing-error analyses, and statistical tests.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix D, including Tables 1–16.

M1.justification: The logit and perplexity fingerprints, cost-band contrastive objective, query encoder, and cost-adjusted nearest-neighbor inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three benchmarks, unseen-LLM scenario, and STEM-to-non-STEM prompt generalization scenario. The category coverage in Table 6 is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains UMR, Thompson, Soft-MoE, Parametric, Pareto-Random, Random, and Oracle. Comparator membership also remains unchanged within the unseen-LLM and OOD comparisons in Tables 2–3.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and D.1 retain the same probe selection, descriptor settings, training schedule, evaluation metrics, and cost definitions. The held-out model split and OOD prompt split are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same descriptor, cost-aware training, cost-band, neighbor-count, penalty, temperature, and router-size ablations. The generalization tests, routing example, selection profiles, and error breakdown are likewise retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds a checklist statement that error bars could not be provided because of computational cost. This is an added uncertainty-reporting disclosure, not evidence of changed runs or procedures: Appendix D.6 retains the same 3,000-prompt paired bootstrap, 5,000 resamples, confidence interval, and McNemar test. The checklist's negative answer on significance reporting conflicts with those retained analyses.

E6.justification: All reported table values and plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains CSCR AUDC values of 0.541, 0.051, and 0.7110 for EmbedLLM, MixInstruct, and RouterBench, respectively; the generalization, ablation, and significance results also match.

T1.justification: The definitions, Lipschitz assumption, excess-risk theorem, directional-alignment lemma, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same cross-entropy and gradient derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scope: compact expert descriptors, cost-aware contrastive routing, efficient inference, and generalization to unseen experts and prompts. The claimed improvement of up to 25% is unchanged.

C2.justification: The new checklist supplies a specific computational-cost explanation for omitting error bars. Existing mechanism interpretations, generalization discussions, and the limitation concerning very large expert pools remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Checklist item 5 newly states that all datasets are open source and promises experimental code after the paper decision. This adds release information without supplying a project-code link or establishing availability. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware details in Appendix D.1 are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and all 105 references retain the same cited research and positioning. The novelty claim relative to existing routing approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments, funding disclosures, and a conference checklist, updates venue and affiliation text, and moves the statistical-significance pointer into the general results paragraph. The scientific exposition and section sequence otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Typesetting and page flow change modestly, including moving Figure 5 from page 8 to page 9 and adjusting surrounding spacing. Figures 1–7 retain identical image content, and Tables 1–16 retain their structures and entries; no scientific display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The scientific contribution and evidence are unchanged. Added funding and planned-code-release disclosures provide limited benefit, but the new checklist introduces inconsistencies: it answers negatively on statistical-significance reporting despite Appendix D.6/Table 16, and directs readers to Section 7 for limitations although that section is Acknowledgments. These additions slightly weaken reporting clarity and internal consistency.
